title: Nucleostemin promotes RAD51 filament assembly on double-stranded DNA to protect stalled replication forks.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the full supplementary archive (1,553,498 bytes, application/zip) and extracted it: it contains exactly one file, gkag773_supplemental_file.pdf (1,750,013 bytes, 19 pages, 77 embedded images). Extracted the text of all 19 pages: pages 1-16 are supplementary figure legends for image panels (microscopy, gels, FRET histograms), page 17 is Supplementary Table S1 with 7 short hairpin RNA (shRNA, a reagent that silences a gene) sequences, page 18 is Supplementary Table S2 listing ~15 antibodies, page 19 is Supplementary Table S3 listing ~14 DNA oligonucleotide sequences. Also checked the paper context tool: no accession numbers anywhere in the text, no text-mined accessions, no GEO/SRA/BioProject/BioSample/dbGaP links, and a Zenodo/Dryad search on the DOI returned nothing.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The Data Availability Statement ('The data underlying this article are available in the article and in its online Supplementary Material') and the methods description of the assays (proximity ligation at replication forks, DNA fiber tract ratios, single-molecule FRET traces analysed with custom Python scripts). The per-cell, per-fiber and per-trajectory numbers behind every figure were read only as summary statements in captions ('>400 cells', '>100 fibers', '>250 total trajectories'); no file containing those measurements exists.

a1_downloadable.note: The supplement downloads freely without login (1.5 MB zip from Europe PMC), but it is a single PDF of figure images plus reagent lists. Nothing that could be called a dataset is deposited in any repository.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FIRST KILLER. There is no label column anywhere, because there is no data table. Every quantity the paper measures (foci per nucleus, IdU:CldU replication tract ratio, FRET efficiency, dwell time) exists only as dots and bars inside figure images; a label would have to be constructed by digitising plots from a PDF.

a3_inputs_present.note: No feature table exists either. The only machine-readable content is ~14 DNA oligonucleotide sequences and 7 shRNA sequences, which are reagent recipes for the experiments, not per-example inputs.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated clearly in the figure captions (foci per nucleus, IdU:CldU tract-length ratio, FRET efficiency 0-1, dwell time in seconds), but they describe pictures of data rather than columns of data.

a5_enough_rows.note: Counted by hand in the three supplementary tables: 7 shRNA rows + ~15 antibody rows + ~14 oligonucleotide rows = ~36 rows of reagent metadata. Against the checklist's ~1,500-row bar this is three orders of magnitude short, and none of those rows carry an outcome.

a6_fits_laptop.note: A 1.7 MB PDF fits anywhere. Trivially true and completely irrelevant, since there is nothing to load.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not assessable: the paper reports only lower bounds ('>100 fibers', '>200 cells', '>250 trajectories') and no file exists against which to check them, so the exact sample size of any experiment cannot be recovered.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not a circularity problem: the underlying measurements are direct physical readouts (fluorescence microscopy, gel densitometry, single-molecule FRET), not another model's predictions. The problem is purely that they were never released in extractable form.

existing_models.name: DeepFRET (deep-learning classifier for single-molecule FRET traces)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved; I saw only the search-result listing (Nature Communications 2020, 'Automatic classification and segmentation of single-molecule fluorescence time traces with deep learning'), not the paper itself.

existing_models.name: DNAi and FiberAI (automated DNA fiber assay image analysis tools)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved beyond search listings (DNAi, Nucleic Acids Research 2026 gkag335, described as open-source; FiberAI, bioRxiv 2020). Both analyse DNA fiber microscopy images, which is the measurement step, not a prediction task.

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: No join is possible: the paper carries no standard identifiers beyond four gene symbols (GNL3, RAD51, MRE11, SMARCAL1) and a handful of reagent catalogue numbers.

controls.positive_control: The paper itself runs good wet-lab controls (anti-biotin antibody pairs as positive, single-antibody and anti-EB1 pairs as negative in the proximity ligation assay), but no computational positive control is definable without data.
controls.negative_control: Not definable - label shuffling needs labels.
controls.external_validation: None. No second dataset measures these quantities for these conditions.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: there is no feature/label table, so no model could be trained or evaluated on this paper's measurements.

plain_idea.one_liner: Considered: use DNA shape near a single/double-stranded junction to predict how strongly RAD51 coats it.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would show the model a DNA substrate (its sequence and the geometry of the junction between single- and double-stranded regions) plus which proteins were added, with roughly 250 single-molecule traces per condition across about a dozen conditions - far too few examples, and not released in any readable form.
plain_idea.predict: How much RAD51, a protein that coats DNA to protect broken or stalled replication sites, assembles on that DNA - measured by single-molecule fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET), a ruler that reports nanometre distance changes as a number between 0 and 1.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Labs studying how cells survive replication stress would like a rule for which DNA shapes RAD51 can coat; but this paper's measurements exist only as pictures, so nothing here supports it.

ml_idea: No viable machine-learning project. The paper is a mechanistic cell-biology and biochemistry study: it shows that nucleostemin (NS/GNL3) accumulates at replication forks stalled by hydroxyurea and helps RAD51 form protective filaments on the double-stranded DNA next to a single/double-stranded junction. All evidence is microscopy images, gels and single-molecule FRET histograms, and the only released data are reagent lists. The nearest adjacent project - learning which DNA junction geometries favour RAD51 filament nucleation from single-molecule traces - would require the raw trace files, which are not deposited; any attempt here would mean digitising bar charts out of a PDF.

effort.compute_note: Measured file sizes only (1.5 MB zip, 1.7 MB PDF). No modelling estimate is meaningful because no feature/label table can be built; hours_to_feature_table is null rather than large because the table cannot be built at any effort from released files.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Download the supplement and list its contents - one 19-page PDF of figures and three reagent tables, roughly 36 machine-readable rows and zero outcome columns. This took two minutes and killed the project.

verdict_reason: No dataset exists: the supplement is one PDF of figure images plus shRNA, antibody and oligonucleotide lists (~36 reagent rows), with no accessions in any repository. A2 fails because every measured outcome - foci counts, replication tract ratios, FRET efficiencies - lives inside plots rather than in a column, and A5 fails by three orders of magnitude. This is a well-executed mechanistic study whose evidence is images, which is exactly the shape of paper that cannot seed an ML project.
